trials.name: Tauriel
trials.population: Patients With Prodromal to Mild Alzheimer's Disease
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline on the CDR-SB
trials.results_summary: Failed to show any evidence of clinical efficacy or modulation of tau PET signal accumulation at any dose. The trial was terminated during the open-label extension period due to this lack of efficacy.

trials.name: Lauriet
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline to Last Visit of Double-Blind Treatment Period in Cognitive Function as Measured by the Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale, Cognitive Subscale, 11-Item Version (ADAS-Cog11)
trials.results_summary: The trial was formally negative on its coprimary endpoints. While it showed a significant slowing of cognitive decline on the ADAS-Cog11, it failed to demonstrate any benefit on the functional coprimary endpoint (ADCS-ADL) or secondary endpoints.

trials.population: Healthy Participants and Participants With Mild-to-Moderate Alzheimer's Disease
trials.primary_endpoint: Number of Participants with Adverse Events
trials.results_summary: Established initial safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of semorinemab to support progression to Phase 2 trials.

related_evidence.description: Publication of the Phase 2 Lauriet trial results demonstrating semorinemab failed to slow functional decline in mild-to-moderate AD.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence for the document's central claim—that semorinemab is safe but clinically ineffective at slowing Alzheimer's disease progression—is strong and definitive. The Phase 2 Tauriel trial failed completely on both primary cognitive/functional outcomes and secondary tau PET biomarkers, leading to the premature termination of its open-label extension. A parallel Phase 2 trial (Lauriet) in a mild-to-moderate population was also formally negative, missing its functional coprimary endpoint despite showing a modest cognitive signal. Genentech has subsequently discontinued clinical development of the drug.
